Prerequisite: A FortiGate wireless controller that manages the FortiAP: the FortiAP discovered and authorized, a FortiAP profile assigned to it, and the SSIDs added to the profile's radios, on a FortiOS release that the FortiAP release notes list as supported
What it enables: Every setting made on the FortiGate (FortiAP profiles, SSIDs, WIDS profiles, and the global wireless controller settings), which the FortiGate pushes to the FortiAP; and static discovery of that controller
How to put it in place: Authorize the FortiAP and assign its profile with config wireless-controller wtp; edit <FORTIAP_SERIAL>; set admin enable; set wtp-profile <PROFILE>; end, and add the SSIDs to each radio with config wireless-controller wtp-profile; edit <PROFILE>; config radio-1; set vap-all manual; set vaps <SSID>; end; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Discovering, authorizing, and deauthorizing FortiAP units", "Creating a FortiAP profile", and "Defining a wireless network interface (SSID)"; FortiAP 7.0.0 to 8.0.0 Release Notes, "Product integration support" (for example, FortiAP 8.0.0 needs FortiOS 8.0.0 and later); FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config wireless-controller wtp and config wireless-controller wtp-profile

Prerequisite: A FortiGate interface (or VLAN) dedicated to the FortiAP units, with an IP address, a DHCP server, and Security Fabric Connection access; for a FortiAP management VLAN, a FortiGate VLAN interface with that VLAN ID, tagged on the switch ports to the FortiAPs
What it enables: CAPWAP discovery and control of the FortiAPs on their own segment, the controller address used for static discovery, and the FortiAP management VLAN
How to put it in place: config system interface; edit <AP_INTERFACE>; set ip <IP> <MASK>; set allowaccess fabric; set role lan; end and config system dhcp server; edit <ID>; set interface <AP_INTERFACE>; set default-gateway <IP>; set netmask <MASK>; end; for a management VLAN, config system interface; edit <AP_MGMT_VLAN>; set interface <AP_INTERFACE>; set vlanid <MGMT_VLAN_ID>; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring the network interface for the AP unit"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config system interface and config system dhcp server; Chapter 14 row *Dedicated FortiGate interface for FortiAP units (CAPWAP access)*

Prerequisite: A WIDS profile assigned to the radios of the FortiAP profile
What it enables: Wireless intrusion detection and rogue AP scanning by the FortiAP radios, including monitor and dedicated scan radios
How to put it in place: config wireless-controller wtp-profile; edit <PROFILE>; config radio-1; set wids-profile <WIDS_PROFILE>; end; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Wireless Intrusion Detection System"; Chapter 14 row *Wireless intrusion detection (WIDS profiles)*

Prerequisite: A reachable organization RADIUS server with a unique shared secret, configured on the FortiGate (for EAP-TLS, see P5)
What it enables: WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise 802.1X authentication, RADIUS MAC authentication and MPSK, dynamic VLAN assignment, NAS-Filter-Rule dynamic ACLs, RadSec, authentication survivability, and external MAC authentication portals
How to put it in place: An organization RADIUS service, then config user radius; edit <RADIUS_SERVER>; set server <RADIUS_IP>; set secret <SECRET>; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring WPA2-Enterprise SSID", "VLAN assignment by RADIUS" (step 1: configure access to the RADIUS server), "MAC-based authentication", "Configure NAS-Filter-Rule attribute to set up dACL", and "RADIUS authentication survivability for 802.1X SSIDs"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config user radius

Prerequisite: PKI: the DoD CA certificates and certificates issued from that PKI to the RADIUS server, the wireless clients, the FortiGate (WiFi and portal server certificates), and any FortiAP that authenticates its WAN port with EAP-TLS
What it enables: EAP-TLS with certificate validation, RadSec server validation, a WiFi certificate and captive-portal server certificate that clients can trust, and EAP-TLS on the FortiAP WAN port
How to put it in place: Import the certificates on the FortiGate in GUI: System > Certificates (Import > CA Certificate, and Import > Local Certificate with its key); load a FortiAP's WAN-port CA certificate, client certificate, and private key from a TFTP server with the FortiAP CLI cw_diag -c wan1x options (or enroll them with P7)
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Replacing WiFi certificate", "Configuring 802.1X supplicant on LAN", and the appendix "FortiAP CLI configuration and diagnostics commands" (cw_diag -c wan1x get-ca-cert, get-client-cert, get-private-key); Chapter 14 rows *WiFi controller certificate for 802.1X and captive portal* and *RADIUS over TLS (RadSec) for WPA2/WPA3-Enterprise authentication*

Prerequisite: An upstream switch port with 802.1X port authentication (with MACsec where MACsec is used) and its authentication server, and the FortiAP's supplicant credentials
What it enables: FortiAP WAN-port 802.1X supplicant, MACsec on the WAN port, and certificate enrollment over the 802.1X WAN port
How to put it in place: Enable 802.1X (and MACsec) on the switch port the FortiAP connects to, with the FortiAP's identity on the authentication server; a switch setting, not a FortiAP one
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring 802.1X supplicant on LAN" (the FortiAP authenticates when connected to a switch port with 802.1X authentication enabled); FortiAP 7.4.3 Release Notes, bug 951641 (MACsec in WAN-port 802.1X authentication; FortiAP works with confidentiality offset 0 or 30)

Prerequisite: An EST or SCEP server reachable from the FortiAPs, issuing certificates from the organization PKI
What it enables: Automatic CA certificate requests by FortiAPs connected over an 802.1X WAN port
How to put it in place: An organization EST or SCEP service; the FortiAP profile then names it (apcfg-auto-cert-est-server or apcfg-auto-cert-scep-url)
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring EST and SCEP servers for CA requests" (FortiAP firmware 7.6.4 or later)

Prerequisite: A reachable TACACS+ server with the FortiAP administrator accounts, configured on the FortiGate
What it enables: Console, SSH, and HTTPS login to the FortiAP with remote accounts
How to put it in place: An organization TACACS+ service, then config user tacacs+; edit <TACACS_SERVER>; set server <TACACS_IP>; set key <KEY>; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Remote TACACS user access for FortiAP management"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config user tacacs+

Prerequisite: A central syslog server or SIEM reachable from the FortiAP units and the FortiGate
What it enables: Off-loading the FortiAP log messages (syslog profile) and the wireless event log the FortiGate records
How to put it in place: An organization syslog server or SIEM; the FortiAPs reach it through the syslog profile, and the FortiGate with config log syslogd setting; set status enable; set server <SYSLOG_IP>; set mode reliable; set enc-algorithm high; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring a Syslog profile"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config log syslogd setting; Chapter 14 rows *Wireless event logging on the FortiGate* and *FortiAP log messages sent to a syslog server*

Prerequisite: A FortiAnalyzer that accepts the logs, reachable from the FortiAP units
What it enables: Local-bridging UTM logs sent in syslog format to the FortiAnalyzer
How to put it in place: An organization FortiAnalyzer (Chapter 12)
Source: FortiAP 7.4.5 and 7.6.1 Release Notes, bug 0471150 (Wi-Fi 6E models only: local-bridging UTM logs sent in syslog format to the FortiAnalyzer as configured by the FortiGate)

Prerequisite: Lightweight UTM on the bridge-mode SSID: a UTM-capable FortiAP and a UTM profile on the SSID
What it enables: UTM logs from local-bridging SSIDs
How to put it in place: config wireless-controller vap; edit <SSID>; set utm-status enable; set utm-profile <UTM_PROFILE>; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Enforcing UTM policies on a local bridge SSID" (not all FortiAPs are UTM capable); FortiAP 7.4.3 Release Notes, bug 951643 (Wi-Fi 6E models); FortiAP 7.6.4 Release Notes, bug 1210169 (FAP-23JK, 241K, 243K, 244K, 441K, and 443K)

Prerequisite: An SNMPv3 manager with the FortiAP MIB and Fortinet Core MIB, configured with the same user, authentication, and privacy settings, and SNMP allowed in the FortiAP profile
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and notifications for managed FortiAP units
How to put it in place: The organization network management system, then config wireless-controller snmp; config user; edit <SNMP_USER>; set notify-hosts <NMS_IP>; set queries enable; end; end and config wireless-controller wtp-profile; edit <PROFILE>; set allowaccess https ssh snmp; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Monitoring FortiAP with SNMP" (SNMP access in FortiAP profiles; the SNMP manager requires the FortiAP MIB and Fortinet Core MIB; local standalone mode does not support FortiAP direct SNMP)

Prerequisite: Fortinet FortiAP firmware for the model, on a supported upgrade path, from FortiGuard or from the Fortinet Support website with its checksum checked
What it enables: FortiAP firmware upgrades from the controller
How to put it in place: Automatic provisioning downloads the latest compatible firmware from FortiGuard; for a manual upgrade, download the image from the Fortinet Support website and check it at Support > Firmware Image Checksum
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "FortiAP unit firmware upgrade"; FortiAP Release Notes, "Upgrade and downgrade information" (for example, FortiAP 8.0.0 supports upgrading from 7.6.3 and later) and "Firmware image checksums"

Prerequisite: An external captive portal server (for example Cisco ISE) that serves the portal over HTTPS
What it enables: External and external-macauth captive portals, and client logout on external captive-portal SSIDs
How to put it in place: An organization portal server; the SSID names it with config wireless-controller vap; edit <SSID>; set external-web <PORTAL_URL>; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring an external captive portal" (including "To configure an external-macauth portal in bridge mode - CLI")

Prerequisite: A firewall user group with the portal or MAC-authentication users (local, RADIUS, or guest users)
What it enables: Captive-portal authentication and RADIUS MAC authentication groups on the SSID
How to put it in place: config user group; edit <GROUP>; set member <USERS>; end, then config wireless-controller vap; edit <SSID>; set selected-usergroups <GROUP>; end (for MAC authentication, set radius-mac-auth-usergroups <GROUP>)
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configuring a FortiGate captive portal" (create a user group) and "Configuring an external captive portal"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config user group

Prerequisite: The VLAN interfaces that dynamic assignment uses, with their DHCP servers and firewall policies, and for bridge-mode SSIDs the VLANs carried on the switch ports to the FortiAPs
What it enables: Dynamic VLAN assignment by RADIUS attribute, by name tag, and by VLAN pool
How to put it in place: config system interface; edit <VLAN_INTERFACE>; set interface <SSID>; set vlanid <VLAN_ID>; end, with a DHCP server and a firewall policy for each VLAN interface
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "VLAN assignment by RADIUS" (create the VLAN interfaces and their DHCP servers, and security policies), "VLAN assignment by Name Tag", and "VLAN assignment by VLAN pool"

Prerequisite: A wireless layer-3 access control list with its rules
What it enables: Layer-3 access control lists on the SSID, including domain-name (FQDN or wildcard) rules
How to put it in place: config wireless-controller access-control-list; edit <ACL>; config layer3-ipv4-rules; edit 1; set dstaddr <ADDRESS>; set action deny; end; end
Source: FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config wireless-controller access-control-list; FortiAP 8.0.0 Release Notes, bug 1196413

Prerequisite: An MPSK profile with its groups and keys
What it enables: MPSK profiles on local-standalone WPA3-SAE SSIDs
How to put it in place: config wireless-controller mpsk-profile; edit <MPSK_PROFILE>; config mpsk-group; edit <GROUP>; config mpsk-key; edit <KEY_NAME>; set passphrase <PASSPHRASE_15_CHARS_MIN>; end; end; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "MPSK profiles"; FortiOS 8.0.1 CLI Reference, config wireless-controller mpsk-profile

Prerequisite: A FortiGuest or FortiAuthenticator server for user MPSK management, configured on the FortiGate as a RADIUS server
What it enables: User MPSK self-registration and management through FortiGuest or FortiAuthenticator
How to put it in place: An organization FortiGuest or FortiAuthenticator, then config user radius; edit <MPSK_SERVER>; set server <SERVER_IP>; set secret <SECRET>; end
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "User self-registration of MPSKs through FortiGuest" (configure the external FortiGuest RADIUS server); FortiAP 7.4.3 Release Notes, bug 1001339

Prerequisite: A mesh-backhaul SSID with WPA3-SAE security on the FortiGate, assigned to the mesh-root FortiAP
What it enables: WPA3-SAE security over the mesh backhaul
How to put it in place: config wireless-controller vap; edit <MESH_SSID>; set mesh-backhaul enable; set security wpa3-sae; end, then add it to the mesh-root FortiAP's profile
Source: FortiAP 7.4.0 Release Notes, "Support WPA3-SAE security over the mesh backhaul" (on the FortiGate, add one mesh-backhaul VAP with security wpa3-sae and assign it to the mesh-root FortiAP); FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Manually configuring a meshed WiFi network"

Prerequisite: An external antenna installed on a FortiAP model that supports external antennas (Fortinet antennas on FAP-432F and FAP-433F; third-party antennas on select models)
What it enables: Transmit power that accounts for the external antenna's gain
How to put it in place: Install the antenna, and select the profile platform that supports it; a hardware choice, not a setting
Source: FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Configure Fortinet external antenna parameters" and "Configure third-party antennas"; FortiAP 7.2.3 and 7.4.0 Release Notes, bug 868839 (FAP-432F and 433F, when the external antenna is installed)

Prerequisite: A FortiAP model that supports the feature, as the release notes state
What it enables: Console port control (applicable models), FIPS mode (not FAP-431F or FAP-433F), the TPM (Wi-Fi 6E models), WAN-port MACsec (Wi-Fi 6E models; Wi-Fi 7 models from 7.6.2), UTM logs to FortiAnalyzer (Wi-Fi 6E models), and WPA3 beacon protection (Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 models)
How to put it in place: Choose the model from the feature's entry in the FortiAP Release Notes ("New features or enhancements", and "Supported models" for the release you run)
Source: FortiAP 7.0.1 Release Notes, bug 719445 (console port on applicable FAP models); FortiAP 7.4.0, bug 268728 (FAP-431F and FAP-433F cannot support FIPS mode); FortiAP 7.4.1, bug 903097 (Wi-Fi 6E models only: TPM); FortiAP 7.4.3, bug 951641, and 7.6.2, bug 1000375 (MACsec); FortiAP 7.4.5, bug 0471150 (Wi-Fi 6E models only: UTM logs); FortiWiFi and FortiAP 8.0.1 Configuration Guide, "Enabling Beacon Protection" (Wi-Fi 6E and Wi-Fi 7 models running FAP 7.6.1 and later)

Prerequisite: FortiOS 8.0.1 on the managing FortiGate
What it enables: The randomized FortiAP login password on authorization, and WPA3 transition-mode SSIDs with different behavior per radio band
How to put it in place: Upgrade the FortiGate to FortiOS 8.0.1 or later
Source: FortiAP 8.0.0 Release Notes, bugs 1084647 and 1294804 (this feature is only supported on FortiOS 8.0.1)
